annotationRationale: Digit subsets correspond uniquely to ordered numerals. Independent inclusion choices count the subsets, and two-set inclusion-exclusion removes the repeated one-digit numbers.
sourceMethod: Follows the official two subset correspondences and overlap subtraction; clarifies the role of zero and why the correspondences omit and repeat no eligible numbers.

review.mathCheck: Increasing-digit numbers correspond to 511 nonempty subsets of digits 1–9. Decreasing-digit numbers correspond to 1022 subsets of digits 0–9 after excluding the empty set and {0}. Exactly nine positive single-digit numbers overlap, giving \(511+1022-9=1524\), choice B. Leading zeros and all possible lengths are handled.
review.sourceMethodCheck: The candidate independently phrases and explains official solution 17 on pages 5–6: the same two subset bijections and subtraction of the nine repeated single-digit numbers.
review.annotationCheck: The assessed bijection and union nodes and supporting multiplication-principle node match their roles. No material omission.
